fatal_errors: The proposed material system is as-received Q235 steel, whereas the target study concerns an APS-deposited AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating on SS316L followed by controlled annealing.
The central intervention—approximately 150 µm HEA coating deposition and 2 h annealing at 400–850 °C, especially the 550 °C optimum—is entirely absent.

The cited FLiBe study supports selective Mn dissolution from a CrMnFeNi HEA at 700 °C; it does not support native iron-oxide passivation of Q235, chloride-induced iron-oxide dissolution, or the proposed room-temperature/high-temperature contrast.
The native-oxide removal control is confounded by adding an alternative inert coating, so differences cannot be attributed specifically to removal or transformation of the native oxide.

The predicted comparison between room-temperature and high-temperature mass change does not reconstruct the target comparisons among uncoated SS316L, as-sprayed coating, and the 550 °C annealed coating under specified acid and molten-salt tests.
explanation: The response addresses the broad theme of oxide-mediated corrosion during aggressive high-temperature salt exposure and proposes measurable SEM/XRD/EDS and gravimetric observations. However, it does not reconstruct the target material, coating, annealing intervention, reference groups, electrochemical conditions, salt mixtures, or reported outcomes. Its mechanism only weakly overlaps the target's eventual oxide-scale degradation by chloride and molten salts, while omitting the dense refined coating, BCC/FCC structure, Al/Cr-rich passive products, sluggish diffusion, and pore/crack penetration. The sole citation is chemically and materially mismatched and therefore cannot substantiate the hypothesis. The experiment also fails to isolate the governing cause because oxide removal and application of an inert coating are combined.
